newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan investors suffer huge foreign bond losses.
newsitem.headline: Japan investors suffer huge foreign bond losses.

text.p: Japanese private investors and brokers carry over 80 billion yen worth of book losses on their holdings of dual currency bonds after a recent steep decline in the dollar against yen, underwriting sources said on Wednesday.

Underwriters estimated the investors are holding about 50.3 billion yen worth of currency losses from investment in dual currency samurais and about 30 billion yen from investment in foreign exchange options-linked dual currency bonds, which were issued in the Euro market.
One underwriting source said that the value of 136 dual currency samurais issued since September 1995, totalling 3.7015 trillion yen, has fallen by nearly a third or 1.0035 trillion yen.

"Most (yen/U.S. dollar) dual-currency samurai bonds which were offered recently with fixed forex rates set around 125 yen are suffering severe losses," a manager at the research department of a major brokerage said.
A total of 825 billion yen worth of dual currency samurai bonds has been issued since January and the forex rates of most of those bonds were fixed at above 120 yen against the dollar.
The dollar fell as low as 111.98 yen on May 20, down some 12 percent from its recent peak of 127.47 set on May 1.
Underwriters said a total of 300 billion yen worth of options-linked dual currency bonds were offered to Japanese investors, with much of them left unsold and held by Japanese brokerages.
"Looking at the volume of options-linked ones, I imagine book losses are roughly 30 billion yen," one underwriter said.
Such options-linked bonds enable bond holders to receive a high coupon rate in yen only if foreign exchange rates stay above levels agreed at the time of the launch.

The coupon of such options-linked bonds, usually set at between four to five percent, is paid in yen, while the bonds, usually with maturities of three to six months, are redeemed in foreign currencies. The so-called "knock-out" level for most of those options had been set at between 113 to 120 yen.

Underwriters said the total amount of book losses could be well above 100 billion yen if other foreign bonds such as dual currency bonds issued in the Euro market or the Eurodollar and Eurosterling bonds had been included.
In the samurai market, there has not been a dual-currency issue since European Investment Bank (EIB) launched 30 billion yen worth of yen/Australian dollar samurais on May 6.
The forex rate for the issue was fixed at 99.04 yen to the Aussie dollar. The Aussie stood at 88.42/52 yen by late Tokyo.
"The EIB issue was left completely unsold. Since the dollar's decline, we' haven't seen a dual currency samurai issue since EIB," an underwriter said.

"Many brokerages have decided to cancel their original plans to offer the dual currency bonds to private investors during the summer bonus season," he said. "I think the dual-currency bond issuing boom or bubble may have already burst."
